## Description

Beyond the basics, the accountants who get the most from AI are the ones who prompt deliberately. This lab-style session teaches a toolkit of reusable prompt patterns (structured prompts, examples, step-by-step reasoning, critique-and-revise, and output formats you can paste straight into Excel or a memo) and applies each to routine accounting deliverables. You will build your own prompt library that you can share with your team.

## Length

8 hours.

## Key Takeaways

Upon completion of this course, you will understand:

- A repeatable method for turning a vague request into a precise prompt
- Core prompt patterns: role and audience, few-shot examples, structured output, chain of thought, and self-review
- How to get consistent, review-ready formatting (tables, bullet summaries, JSON/CSV) from an LLM
- How to iterate: diagnose why a prompt failed and improve it
- How to build, document and share a team prompt library, including version notes and known limitations

## Workflows We Will Work Through

Hands-on exercises use realistic, simulated (never confidential) data. Examples across functions and industries include:

- Month-end close: first-draft flux commentary and a close-status summary
- Accounts payable and receivable: classify and explain unusual transactions from a sample list
- Technical accounting: structure a position memo outline, including facts, issue, analysis and conclusion
- Audit: draft test procedures and documentation language from a control description
- Tax and compliance: build a checklist from a regulatory update
- Management reporting: tailor the same results for a CFO, a board and a department head

Exercises are tool-agnostic. You can follow along with Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot or ChatGPT, whichever your organization permits.

## Target Audience

- **Accountants who already use AI occasionally** and want more consistent, higher-quality results
- **Team leads and managers** who want to standardize good AI habits across a team
- **Finance professionals in any function**, including FP&A, controllership, audit, tax and treasury

## Prerequisite(s)

Basic experience using an LLM tool is expected. Completing "AI Foundations for Accountants" is recommended but not required.
